topics.title: Setting Up Automatic SMS Import
topics.description: Follow this step-by-step guide to set up automatic transaction SMS import in the CCReward iOS app. This automation allows your credit card transaction SMS messages to be imported directly into the app without any manual input.

steps.description: Find the Shortcuts App: Look for the Shortcuts app icon on your iPhone's home screen.
steps.alt: Shortcuts app icon on iOS home screen
steps.tip: If you can't find the Shortcuts app, you may need to download it from the App Store.

steps.description: Start a New Automation: Open the Shortcuts app. Tap the 'Automation' button at the bottom (middle icon). Tap the '+' sign in the top-right corner.
steps.caption: The Automation tab is the second icon in the bottom navigation.

steps.description: Choose the Message Trigger: In the search bar at the top, type 'Message'. Select 'Message' from the options that appear.
steps.alt: Plus button to create a new automation
steps.tip: If you don't see the plus icon, you may need to scroll to the top of the screen.

steps.description: Set Up the 'When': You'll see options like 'Sender', 'Message Contains'. Tap on 'Message Contains' to specify the kind of message to look for.
steps.caption: Personal automations run on your device.

steps.description: It should open a popup asking 'Message Contains'
steps.tip: This trigger will run the automation whenever you receive specific text messages.

steps.description: Enter Your Bank's Message Text: Type the specific phrase your bank uses in its transaction SMS alerts (e.g., 'spent using ICICI Bank Card').
details: ICICI: spent using ICICI Bank Card
HDFC: spent on HDFC Bank Card
IDFC: spent on your IDFC FIRST Bank Credit Card ending
SBI: spent on your SBI Credit Card ending
Kotak: spent on Kotak Bank Card
RBL: on RBL Bank credit card
AU: spent on AU Bank Credit Card
BOB: is spent on your BOBCARD ending
Federal: spent on your credit card ending with
SC: Thank you for using StanChart Credit Card No
YesBank: spent on YES BANK Card
steps.alt: Message trigger configuration screen showing message contains field
steps.caption: This is where you enter the specific text that identifies your bank messages.

steps.alt: Message contains field selection with example
steps.tip: Run Immediately ensures the automation happens without asking you each time.

steps.description: choose 'New Blank Automation' under Get Started
In the 'Search Actions' bar at the bottom, type 'ccreward'.
steps.tip: Make sure you have the CCReward app installed.

steps.description: Tap on 'Process Bank Transaction' from the CCReward actions shown.
steps.alt: Selecting the Process Bank Transaction action
steps.caption: This action sends the SMS to the CCReward app.

steps.description: Tap the 'Message Text' part of the action you just added (it might say 'Import bank transaction from message').
steps.alt: Tapping on the Message Text placeholder

steps.description: Keyboard should open now and show Select Variable, Scroll 'Select Variable' the right until see 'Shortcut Input'. Tap it.
steps.alt: Process Bank Transaction action ready for input
steps.caption: This prepares the action to use the SMS text.

steps.alt: Setting Shortcut Input as the variable
steps.tip: This passes the SMS text to the CCReward app. You should find new SMS in the CCReward calculator page.

troubleshooting: If transactions aren't importing, make sure 'Run without asking' is enabled in the automation settings
Check that you've correctly copied the exact message pattern text for your bank
Ensure CCReward app is updated to the latest version
Sometimes bank message formats may vary; you might need to adjust the text pattern slightly
If you're not receiving transaction notifications, check that your bank has SMS alerts enabled for your credit card
Make sure you don't have message filtering enabled that could block bank SMS messages
Support for additional banks including IndusInd, Canara, DBS, OneCard, and IDBI coming soon
